decisions.quote:
Our paper conducts an independent replication and
       two out-of-sample tests with three datasets (US 1964 to 1999, US
       2000 to 2016, and Japan 1978 to 2012), six versions of the LCAPM,
       and eight test portfolios.
decisions.reason: For the resolved original Acharya and Pedersen (2005, DOI 10.1016/j.jfineco.2004.06.007), addressing the parent hybrid-workflow objection: although the authors initially mention 'quantitative replication' (recovering exact original coefficients) as an interest, they explicitly state in Section 1 (p. 77) that AP did not provide full details of the estimation procedure so quantitative coefficient recovery is infeasible, and they instead independently reconstruct the 1964–1999 US sample from CRSP/COMPUSTAT and re-test the LCAPM hypotheses across both that reconstructed sample and two new out-of-sample datasets (US 2000–2016 and Japan 1978–2012 from the Nikkei Financial Database). Because the study re-tests the published empirical claim using new samples rather than re-analyzing the original authors' data or code, it is a replication under the codebook.

decisions.quote:
In summary, from the above results (and also from Holden and Nam (2018)),
although we observe improvements in a fit of the AP LCAPM over the CAPM
in terms of R2 , one has to conclude that the LCAPM does not satisfy either of
the one-variable LCAPM test and the two-variable LCAPM test.
decisions.reason: Addressing the parent objection on the dependent outcome across the hybrid design: across the reconstructed 1964–1999 US sample (7/16 one-variable and 3/24 two-variable tests passed), the 2000–2016 US sample (8/16 and 1/24 passed), and the 1978–2012 Japanese sample (0/16 and 0/24 passed), the shipped outcome relies on the raw pass-rate percentages (36.0% and 5.2%), which the codebook states do not by themselves establish a mixed outcome. Under Codebook Rule 1 and the multi-sample aggregation rule, the authors' explicit overall verdict synthesizing all tests—that 'one has to conclude that the LCAPM does not satisfy either of the one-variable LCAPM test and the two-variable LCAPM test'—governs and establishes a failed replication outcome.
